APP_ENV.notes: Switches logs to JSON on stdout and is stamped on all telemetry as `deployment.environment.name`. In nest-api, `development` also adds local servers to the OpenAPI document.

node-worker:APP_ENV.notes: `production` logs JSON to stdout; anything else pretty-prints when the pretty printer is installed. Stamped on telemetry as `deployment.environment.name`.

APP_NAME.notes: Used in emails, the Swagger title and better-auth. Set by `--name`.

APP_HOST.notes: The address the server binds to. `127.0.0.1` would make it unreachable from outside the container.

PORT.production: The port the process listens on (nest-api: the container's exposed port).
PORT.notes: Changing it after generation means changing `SERVER_HOST` and `BETTER_AUTH_URL` too; `--port` at generation does all three.

react-app:PORT.production: Not used: production is a static bundle served by nginx on port 80.
react-app:PORT.notes: The dev server's port. It's strict: a port in use makes Vite exit instead of moving.

react-monorepo:PORT.production: Not used: each app's image serves on port 80.
react-monorepo:PORT.notes: Each app's dev server port (landing 3000, auth 3001, client 3002, admin 3003). Change one and update the sibling `VITE_APP_*_HOST` values.

SERVER_HOST.notes: Used in email links, the OpenAPI servers list and the `/health` HTTP check, which calls it from inside the container, so it must resolve there.

FRONTEND_HOST.notes: Trusted by auth and allowed by CORS. The welcome email links to it. Other front-end origins go in `MISC_CORS_ORIGINS`.

MISC_CORS_ORIGINS.production: Every other front-end origin, comma-separated; empty for a single front end.
MISC_CORS_ORIGINS.notes: A full origin (`http://localhost:3001`) is used as written; a bare hostname (`example.com`) expands to https origins for it and its `auth.`, `app.` and `admin.` subdomains. See [Auth, cookies and CORS](/services/auth-domains/).

DATABASE_URL.notes: A worker's value must be the API's database. URL-encode special characters in the password. See [PostgreSQL](/services/postgres/).

BETTER_AUTH_SECRET.notes: Signs sessions. The example value boots, but anyone reading the template knows it. Changing it signs every user out.

BETTER_AUTH_URL.notes: better-auth's base URL: OAuth callbacks are `<this>/auth/callback/<provider>`.

BETTER_AUTH_COOKIE_DOMAIN.production: Empty for a single front-end origin; `.example.com` to share one login across subdomains.
BETTER_AUTH_COOKIE_DOMAIN.notes: The domain must cover the host the browser talks to, or the cookie is silently dropped and every sign-in bounces. See [Auth, cookies and CORS](/services/auth-domains/).

BETTER_AUTH_COOKIE_PREFIX.production: Keep the generated value (the project name).
BETTER_AUTH_COOKIE_PREFIX.notes: Distinguishes this project's cookies from others on the same parent domain. The runtime and tooling instances must agree.

SUPERUSER_EMAIL.notes: `yarn db:seed` creates this user, verified, with the `superuser` role. Seeding again fails on the existing email.

SUPERUSER_PASSWORD.production: A strong password, changed after first sign-in.

OAUTH_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID.source: Google Cloud console → Credentials. See [Google sign-in](/services/google-oauth/).
OAUTH_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID.notes: Empty disables Google sign-in (the button fails).

LOG_LEVEL.notes: pino levels: `trace`, `debug`, `info`, `warn`, `error`, `fatal`, `silent`. An empty value fails validation in nest-api.

OPENOBSERVE_URL.notes: Telemetry is on only when the URL, org and token are all set. See [OpenObserve](/services/openobserve/).

OPENOBSERVE_ORG.source: OpenObserve → organization settings (or the org segment of its URLs).

OPENOBSERVE_TOKEN.notes: Write-only, but secret: never use it in a browser app (front ends use a RUM token).

OTEL_SERVICE_NAME.notes: The service name on every span, and the default stream name, so each service gets its own stream.

HEALTH_HEAP_MAX_MB.production: Below the container's memory limit, e.g. 75% of it.
HEALTH_HEAP_MAX_MB.notes: Past it, `/health` reports down and orchestrators restart the instance.

HEALTH_DISK_THRESHOLD.production: The fraction of the volume that may be used, e.g. `0.9`.

HEALTH_DISK_PATH.production: The volume to watch: `/`, or where logs and uploads are written.

BASIC_AUTH_USER.notes: Guards `/docs`, `/openapi`, `/openapi-json` and `/dashboard`. Front ends' `yarn gen` uses it as `API_DOC_USER`.

BASIC_AUTH_PASS.production: A strong password, not the example's.

REDIS_HOST.production: Your Redis host; identical on the API and every worker.
REDIS_HOST.notes: A worker on a different Redis connects fine and never receives a job. See [Redis](/services/redis/).

REDIS_USER.production: An ACL user, if your Redis uses them.

SMTP_PORT.notes: No other value validates. For a local catcher, map it to 587.

SMTP_USER.notes: Required and empty by default: the API won't start until it's set.

SMTP_PASSWORD.production: The SMTP password or API key.

SMTP_FROM.production: `Name <no-reply@your-domain>`, on a domain with SPF, DKIM and DMARC.
SMTP_FROM.notes: Without those records, verification emails land in spam, and new users can't sign in until they verify.

SMTP_SUPPORT_EMAIL.notes: Shown in the welcome email; keep it equal to a landing site's `VITE_APP_SUPPORT_EMAIL`.

S3_ENDPOINT.production: The endpoint URL, even on AWS: `https://s3.<region>.amazonaws.com`.
S3_ENDPOINT.notes: Also the prefix of stored file URLs: empty, they're relative and browsers can't load them. See [Object storage](/services/s3/).

S3_BUCKET_NAME.notes: Must allow object ACLs: uploads outside the private folders are `public-read`.

S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID.production: An access key for the bucket.

TEMPORAL_NAMESPACE.production: The project's namespace, the same on the API and its workers.

TEMPORAL_TASK_QUEUE.notes: API: where workflows are started. Worker: the queue it polls. A mismatch is silent: workflows wait forever.

py-worker:TEMPORAL_TASK_QUEUE.notes: Keep Python workflows on a queue no Node worker polls: a workflow task handed to a worker that doesn't know the type fails and retries. The API starts Python workflows on this queue.

TEMPORAL_TLS_CA.production: The CA that signed the server's certificate, as PEM; empty if it's publicly trusted.
TEMPORAL_TLS_CA.notes: Escaped `\n` are accepted, so it fits on one line.

TEMPORAL_TLS_CERT.production: The project's client certificate, as PEM.
TEMPORAL_TLS_CERT.source: Issued by whoever runs your Temporal (the gateway's CA).
TEMPORAL_TLS_CERT.notes: Set it together with `TEMPORAL_TLS_KEY`, or startup fails.

TEMPORAL_TLS_KEY.production: The client certificate's private key, as PEM.
TEMPORAL_TLS_KEY.notes: A secret: keep it in your secret store.

RATE_LIMIT_ENABLED.notes: Off in `.env.test` so specs don't share a rate-limit window.

RATE_LIMIT_TTL.production: The window for app routes, in **milliseconds** (default 60000).

RATE_LIMIT_MAX.production: Requests per window per client IP on app routes (default 120).

RATE_LIMIT_AUTH_WINDOW.notes: Sign-in, sign-up and password routes also have stricter built-in rules.

RATE_LIMIT_AUTH_MAX.production: Requests per auth window per client IP (default 100).

RATE_LIMIT_IP_HEADERS.production: The header your reverse proxy sets to the client's IP (`x-forwarded-for`, `cf-connecting-ip`, …).
RATE_LIMIT_IP_HEADERS.notes: Behind a proxy without it, every client shares one bucket, and if no IP resolves, better-auth stops rate limiting. Exposed directly, a client can spoof it.

GROWTHBOOK_API_HOST.notes: Required with `feature-flags` and empty by default. See [GrowthBook](/services/growthbook/).

PUPPETEER_EXECUTABLE_PATH.production: Set by the Docker image (`/usr/bin/chromium` or `/usr/bin/chromium-browser`).
PUPPETEER_EXECUTABLE_PATH.notes: Empty uses Puppeteer's own Chromium, which the image doesn't download.

HOME_PATH.notes: Required and absolute: logs, `input/` and `output/` resolve beneath it.

DB_HOST.notes: Must be the API's database. See [PostgreSQL](/services/postgres/).

DB_USER.production: A database user with access to the tables this worker uses.

VITE_APP_API_URL.production: The API's public URL, as a **build argument**.
VITE_APP_API_URL.notes: Compiled into the bundle. Auth lives at `<this>/auth`, and requests to it carry the `traceparent` header.

VITE_APP_ALLOWED_HOSTS.notes: Hostnames the dev server answers beyond localhost: a tunnel or `*.lvh.me`.

VITE_OPENOBSERVE_URL.production: Your OpenObserve instance, as a build argument.
VITE_OPENOBSERVE_URL.notes: Telemetry is on only when the URL, org and client token are all set.

VITE_OPENOBSERVE_ORG.production: The project's organization identifier, as a build argument.

VITE_OPENOBSERVE_CLIENT_TOKEN.production: A RUM token, as a build argument.
VITE_OPENOBSERVE_CLIENT_TOKEN.notes: Public by design (write-only). Never the back ends' ingestion token. The instance must list this origin in `ZO_CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS`.

VITE_APP_SITE_URL.production: The canonical public origin, as a build argument.
VITE_APP_SITE_URL.notes: Must equal `PRODUCTION_ORIGIN` in `src/features/seo/routes.ts`; any other value builds as `noindex` with a disallowing robots.txt, so previews can't outrank production.

VITE_APP_SUPPORT_EMAIL.production: A monitored security and support address, as a build argument.
VITE_APP_SUPPORT_EMAIL.notes: Published in `/.well-known/security.txt`; empty skips the file.

API_DOC_URL.production: Not used in production: only by `yarn gen`.

VITE_APP_LANDING.production: The landing site's origin, e.g. `https://example.com`, as a build argument.
VITE_APP_LANDING.notes: Every app lists its siblings: they're the trusted redirect targets. The auth app links to its terms and privacy pages.

VITE_APP_CLIENT_HOST.notes: Where the auth app sends people after sign-in by default.
